details:
Outpost Odyssey — Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Outpost Odyssey is a browser-based educational mission simulation designed to help students understand the challenges of operating a future space outpost. The player takes the role of a mission commander and manages limited resources such as oxygen, water, food, energy, radiation protection, and crew health while progressing through a multi-day mission.

The game uses a simple decision-based system. Players monitor the condition of the outpost, perform operations such as recycling water, growing crops, cleaning solar panels, improving radiation protection, and allowing crew rest, and respond to unexpected mission alerts. Each decision changes the available resources, helping players understand the relationship between limited resources, risk, and mission success.

The project is intended to make space science more interactive and accessible. Instead of only learning about life-support systems and space missions theoretically, students can experiment with decisions and immediately observe their consequences. The project encourages problem-solving, resource management, risk assessment, and STEM learning.

The prototype was developed as a web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The interface, resource dashboard, mission operations, decision scenarios, and game logic are implemented for browser-based interaction. The project is hosted using GitHub Pages, making the demonstration publicly accessible through a web browser.

The creative aspect of Outpost Odyssey is its combination of a space mission dashboard with an interactive decision-making game. The design focuses on keeping the controls simple enough for beginners while still representing important concepts involved in sustaining a crew in a remote environment. The project also uses simulated resource changes so learners can explore different strategies without requiring real spacecraft hardware or complex systems.
